t: authd: SSH session with another account's UID via lost in-memory ID reservation after authd restart
d: In authd before 0.7.2, an improper access control vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to complete a first-time SSH login with another account's UID and incorrect primary GID, and to read or modify files owned by that account. This allows an attacker to access another account's data, potentially enabling account takeover or privilege escalation.

t: metasfresh through 5.175 SQL Injection via tableName Parameter in DebugRestController
d: metasfresh through 5.175 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the stressTest_massCacheInvalidation handler of DebugRestController, which concatenates the caller-supplied tableName request parameter into SELECT statements without parameterization or validation and only checks that the caller is authenticated. Authenticated WebUI users with any role can send GET requests to /rest/api/debug/stressTest/massCacheInvalidation with SQL in the tableName parameter to run time-based and error-based blind queries against the PostgreSQL database, extracting sensitive ERP data such as user credentials and financial records while also degrading availability through sleep payloads.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex Debug Interface With Improper Access Control Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex Debug Interface With Improper Access Control Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows physically present attackers to bypass authentication on affected ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the serial debug interface. The issue results from the lack of access control prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-28997.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex busybox Unnecessary Privileges Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex busybox Unnecessary Privileges Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the busybox binary. The issue results from the setuid flag being set. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29090.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex wpa_passphrase Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex wpa_passphrase Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the PSK parameter passed to the wpa_passphrase endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29000.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex ssh Hard-coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex ssh Hard-coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the ssh service, which listens on TCP port 22 by default. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-28996.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex uploadsm filetype Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex uploadsm filetype Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of the filetype parameter passed to the uploadsm endpoint. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to write an arbitrary file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29096.

t: ChargePoint Home Flex dwnldlogsm tar Command Injection Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
d: ChargePoint Home Flex dwnldlogsm tar Command Injection Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the tar function. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29057.

t: D-Link R32 DHMAPI Action httpd SetDeviceSettings os command injection
d: A vulnerability has been found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. The impacted element is the function SetDeviceSettings of the file /usr/bin/httpd of the component DHMAPI Action Handler. Such manipulation of the argument TZLocation leads to os command injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

t: Improper Neutralization of Quoting Syntax in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute quick actions through Service Desk emails due to improper input sanitization.

t: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 14.4 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to cause denial of service due to unconstrained backtracking in regular expression evaluation.

t: Incorrect Authorization in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a fine-grained personal access token to read work items in projects or groups they have access to but that were not granted to the token due to incorrect authorization checks.

t: RustDesk Client for Windows reg_recovery Missing Authorization Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
d: RustDesk Client for Windows reg_recovery Missing Authorization Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of RustDesk Client for Windows. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the main IPC endpoint exposed by the RustDesk service. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-34805.

t: Out-of-bounds read in it51xxx I2C target FIFO ISR on oversized read transaction
d: The ITE it51xxx I2C driver, when operating as an I2C target (slave) in buffer mode (CONFIG_I2C_TARGET + CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_BUFFER_MODE), transmits response data from the fixed-size data->target_out_buffer inside its target FIFO interrupt handler target_i2c_isr_fifo() in drivers/i2c/i2c_ite_it51xxx.c. On every data interrupt of a host read transaction the handler pushes a fixed 16 bytes from target_out_buffer[i + data->r_index] into the hardware FIFO and then advances data->r_index by 16, without ever checking that index against the size of the buffer. data->r_index is reset to zero only on a STOP or timeout condition, so within a single transaction it only accumulates. An I2C host that keeps clocking read bytes without issuing STOP drives data->r_index past the end of the buffer after sixteen interrupts (default CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_IT51XXX_MAX_BUF_SIZE = 256 bytes), and every interrupt after that reads 16 bytes from beyond target_out_buffer and places them on the bus. What follows the buffer in the driver's device data structure is data->target_shared_fifo and the remaining static device state, so a sufficiently long read transaction streams adjacent firmware memory to the host. The same handler, and the shared-FIFO arm of target_i2c_isr_pio(), also declare the transfer length uninitialised and invoke the optional buf_read_requested() callback without checking that it is registered. A target that supplies no read callback leaves the source pointer NULL and the length indeterminate; when that length compares below the destination size, memcpy() runs with a NULL source. Because the transmit path feeds the FIFO whether or not the callback provided data, such a target also places whatever the previous request left in the buffer onto the bus. The trigger is a malicious or misbehaving I2C master on the same bus (for example a compromised application processor or a rogue device on an exposed I2C bus); no software privilege on the victim is required and the handler runs in the target's kernel/firmware context. The disclosed bytes are not attacker-chosen, but their extent is: the host controls how long the transaction runs and therefore how far past the buffer the driver reads. This is the read-direction counterpart of CVE-2026-14986, which closed the write direction of the same routine without adding the matching bound on the read path.

t: Stack buffer overflow in Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver UART RX handler
d: The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default). A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. The ISR then writes that many attacker-supplied bytes past the end of the stack buffer. The existing length check in r502a_validate_rx_packet() runs only after the data has been written, so it does not prevent the overflow. Every sensor transaction is affected, including the ones issued by fps_init() during device initialization. The result is a stack overwrite with attacker-controlled length and content in the calling thread. This can corrupt control data and may lead to arbitrary code execution on the host MCU, which would undermine any function the fingerprint sensor is meant to protect. The fix validates the declared length against CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE as soon as the header is complete and aborts the reception if it is out of range.

t: Stack use-after-return on RX timeout in Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver
d: The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) points drv_data->rx_buf.data at an rx_packet buffer on the caller's stack and enables the UART RX interrupt before waiting 1500 ms for a reply. When the wait timed out, transceive_packet() returned -ETIMEDOUT but left the RX interrupt enabled and rx_buf.data still pointing at the caller's buffer. Once the caller's frame has returned, any bytes that arrive late on the UART are written by the interrupt handler uart_cb_handler() through the dangling pointer into stack memory that the thread has since reused. The bytes come from the device on the other end of the UART. An attacker with physical access who replaces or impersonates the fingerprint module can trigger this by delaying a reply past the timeout and then sending a packet. A slow or faulty genuine module can also trigger it by accident. The result is a write of attacker-chosen bytes into a live thread stack. The write length comes from the header of the late packet. Commit 96968fac22b, which landed together with this fix, bounds it to a header plus CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE bytes; affected releases do not have that bound. This can crash the device and may allow control-flow hijacking, depending on what occupies the reused stack region. The fix disables the RX interrupt, resets the RX semaphore and clears rx_buf.data on timeout, and the interrupt handler now refuses to write when no receive buffer is armed.

t: PWM capture syscall leaves callback armed on a dead kernel stack frame when called with K_NO_WAIT
d: z_impl_pwm_capture_cycles() in drivers/pwm/pwm_capture.c stores its capture context (struct z_pwm_capture_cb_data, including a struct k_sem) on its own stack and registers a pointer to it as the driver capture callback's user_data. When called with a K_NO_WAIT timeout, k_sem_take() returns -EBUSY, which the function did not handle: it fell through, returned the uninitialized status field, copied uninitialized period/pulse values to the caller when that status happened to be zero, and returned without disabling the capture or clearing the callback. pwm_capture_cycles() is a system call, and z_vrfy_pwm_capture_cycles() passes the caller's timeout through unchanged. With CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_PWM_CAPTURE enabled, an unprivileged user-mode thread that has been granted access to a capture-capable PWM device can pass K_NO_WAIT to trigger the defect. Without userspace the function is only reachable from trusted application code. The uninitialized values come from the thread's privileged (kernel) stack, so a user-mode caller can read up to 8 bytes of stale kernel stack memory per call. More seriously, when the capture later completes, the driver ISR invokes z_pwm_capture_cycles_callback() with the dangling pointer. The callback writes into the expired kernel stack region and calls k_sem_give() on whatever memory now occupies it, which can corrupt live kernel stack frames and make the scheduler walk a forged wait queue. The result is kernel memory corruption from interrupt context, leading at least to a crash and possibly to privilege escalation out of the userspace sandbox. The fix rejects K_NO_WAIT with -EINVAL before any capture is configured.

t: AutoGPT: AutoPilot fails to clean up temporary media files from block executions, allowing executor disk exhaustion
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.46 through 0.11.1, AutoPilot does not remove the media files that its block runs write to the executor's disk, leading to exhaustion. A signed-in user who can use AutoPilot can grow the temporary storage used by AutoPilot's tool process by about 1 GiB per chat. Once that filesystem is full, file handling fails for every user served by that executor and for anything else writing to the same disk. No other user's data is read or changed. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.

t: D-Link R32 DHMAPI Action SetTimeSettings os command injection
d: A flaw has been found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. The affected element is the function SetTimeSettings of the component DHMAPI Action Handler. This manipulation of the argument TZLocation causes os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

t: EduardoPires EquinoxProject JWT Bearer Authentication appsettings.Development.json BuildToken hard-coded credentials
d: A weakness has been identified in EduardoPires EquinoxProject up to 1.10. This vulnerability affects the function BuildToken of the file src/Equinox.Services.Api/appsettings.Development.json of the component JWT Bearer Authentication. This manipulation of the argument SecretKey with the input fmFGn5agHZkuG2N0e1zaEJIQtGVoNN5P causes hard-coded credentials. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

t: Improper input validation in the AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3
d: Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions. Because any user permitted to run the runbook selects which revision to run, this issue remains reachable in an affected Region until earlier revisions can no longer be run there. AWS is deprecating all revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) in every Region and partition beginning January 15, 2027; until deprecation, earlier revisions remain runnable, so upgrading alone is not sufficient. To remediate this issue: 1. Run the latest revision of the runbook. The latest revision is the fixed revision in every Region where the runbook is available, and its revision number varies by Region. To find it, run aws ssm describe-document --name AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 --region <region> --query "Document.LatestVersion". Update any Automation executions, State Manager associations, AWS Config remediation configurations, or other automations pinned to an earlier revision to use the latest revision. 2. Until earlier revisions are removed in your Region, either keep untrusted users from running earlier revisions of the runbook, or keep a trusted Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in every Region. Earlier revisions inject only when they create this document, so while a trusted one exists, this path is closed in that Region. 3. Review your Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in any Region where it was first created by an earlier revision of this runbook, not by you. To check, look for any run of this runbook that failed with "DOCUMENT CREATE OR UPDATE FAILED." An injected run always fails with this error. You can also compare the creation date of the document's first version with the start times of runs of this runbook in that Region. Check the document for settings you did not configure, especially shellProfile, Run As (runAsEnabled, runAsDefaultUser), maxSessionDuration, idleSessionTimeout, and the logging destination fields. The fixed runbook updates only the S3 bucket and prefix fields of an existing preferences document, so settings injected earlier remain until you remove them. If you find unexpected settings, restore your trusted preferences and review instances on which Session Manager sessions were started while those settings were active. The AWS Security Bulletin includes commands for this review.

t: AutoGPT: Sandbox file extraction has no cumulative byte or file-count limit
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.6.49 before 0.11.0, sandbox file extraction has no cumulative byte or file-count limit. A user who can run a code-execution block that extracts files can exhaust the memory of the shared workflow executor, interrupting other users' runs on it. Each file was allowed up to 50 MB based on a size that the sandbox itself reported. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0 Command Execution via Auto-Approved git blame
d: DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0 contains a command execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands without user approval because the shellsafe classifier treats git blame and git whatchanged as read-only. Attackers can plant a diff textconv driver in .gitattributes and .git/config so that git blame, triggered via prompt injection or routine use, executes attacker-chosen commands with the user's privileges, exposing stored provider API keys and session history.

t: llama.cpp b7118 before b12604 Integer Underflow in Grammar Parser parse_sequence
d: llama.cpp from b7118 before b12604 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in llama_grammar_parser::parse_sequence() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service by supplying GBNF repetitions with max lower than min. Attackers can send a grammar like {5,2} in the grammar field of a llama-server /completion request, wrapping n_opt to generate endless repetition rules that hang the process and exhaust memory.

t: cron-parser through 5.10.0 Unbounded Memory Allocation via CronExpressionParser.parse()
d: Cron-parser through 5.10.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in CronExpressionParser.parse() that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by supplying oversized cron fields. Attackers can submit a roughly 1.6 MB expression of repeated wildcard tokens that expand into huge arrays, exhausting the V8 heap and crashing the Node.js process.

t: ToolJet 3.16.0 before 3.20.256 Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Bypass
d: ToolJet from 3.16.0 before 3.20.256 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability in StripeWebhookGuard that validates webhooks against a self-generated signature instead of the Stripe-Signature header. Unauthenticated attackers can post forged Stripe events to the POST /api/organization/payment/webhooks route to activate subscriptions, generate licenses, change plans or seats, and add AI credits without payment.

t: paramz through 0.10.0 Insecure Deserialization RCE via load()
d: paramz through 0.10.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted model files to paramz.load(), which calls pickle.load() without restrictions. Attackers can embed objects whose __reduce__ method returns callables like exec or os.system in shared paramz or GPy model files to run code with the victim's privileges.

t: Wallos before 5.11.2 Infinite Loop via Zero Subscription Frequency
d: Wallos before 5.11.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability that allows authenticated users or API key holders to exhaust server resources by storing subscriptions with a frequency of 0. Attackers can trigger renew.php or get_monthly_cost.php to loop forever on a P0D interval, pinning PHP workers and hanging the next-payment cron job for all users.

t: BookStack before 26.09.3 Incorrect Authorization via Chapter and Book Conversion
d: BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editors to permanently delete recycle bin content by converting chapters to books or books to shelves. Attackers can trigger TrashCan::destroyEntity() through the conversion actions to force-delete soft-deleted children, revisions and attachments, including content deleted by other users, preventing restoration.

t: Leptonica 1.79.0 through 1.87.0 Heap Buffer Overflow via l_byteaInitFromStream()
d: Leptonica 1.79.0 through 1.87.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in l_byteaInitFromStream() that allows attackers to write past a heap buffer by supplying oversized input. Attackers can provide a file larger than 1,000,000,000 bytes, causing l_byteaCreate() to allocate a 201-byte buffer before memcpy copies the full stream size, crashing the application.

t: Chatwoot before 4.20.0 Missing Authentication in Bandwidth SMS Webhook
d: Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the Bandwidth SMS webhook endpoint POST /webhooks/sms/:phone_number that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit forged SMS events. Attackers who know an inbox phone number can set the 'to' field to inject inbound messages with forged sender numbers or forge delivery status updates.

t: Chatwoot before 4.20.0 Cross-Account Inbox Reference via Integration Hook Creation
d: Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows account administrators to attach integration hooks to other accounts' inboxes by supplying a foreign inbox_id. Attackers can create a Dialogflow hook referencing a victim inbox, leaving its new conversations stuck as pending awaiting a bot, and enumerate inbox IDs to disclose inbox names.

t: Loginizer before 2.1.4 Brute-Force Lockout Bypass via Non-ASCII Request URL Bytes
d: Loginizer before 2.1.4 contains a brute-force lockout bypass vulnerability in loginizer_login_failed() that allows unauthenticated attackers to avoid failed-attempt recording via non-ASCII URL bytes. Attackers can append invalid UTF-8 or 4-byte sequences to wp-login.php or xmlrpc.php request URLs, causing the log INSERT to fail and enabling unlimited password guessing without lockout or email notification.

t: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 Use-After-Free via xmlValidatePopElement
d: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement because xmlCtxtReset frees the DTD without popping stale validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document ending inside an element to an application reusing a DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads, causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error messages.

t: libxml2 through 2.15.4 Use-After-Free in xmlFreeNode via reader->faketext
d: libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by triggering xmlFreeNode on a stale reader->faketext node after xmlTextReader reuse. Attackers can supply XML containing a namespace declaration to applications that read its value and reuse the reader, causing a freed document's dictionary read and process crash.

t: libxml2 2.13.0 through 2.15.4 Denial of Service via xmlTextReaderSetup Unreset Error State
d: libxml2 2.13.0 through 2.15.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability because xmlTextReaderSetup does not reset reader->state when a reader is reused. Attackers can submit one malformed XML document to an application reusing a single reader, causing every later document to be rejected until the reader is recreated.

t: GEOS 3.13.0 before 3.15.1 Uncontrolled Recursion in RectangleContains::isContainedInBoundary
d: GEOS 3.13.0 before 3.15.1 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in RectangleContains::isContainedInBoundary that recurses indefinitely on curved geometries returned by getGeometryN. Attackers can supply crafted WKT or WKB CircularString, CompoundCurve, or CurvePolygon geometries tested via PreparedGeometry::contains or GEOSPreparedContains against a prepared rectangle to crash the process with a stack overflow.

t: Boost.JSON 1.84.0 through 1.92.0 Information Exposure via parser_for reset()
d: Boost.JSON 1.84.0 through 1.92.0 contains an information exposure vulnerability because parser_for reset() does not reset nested parse_into handlers, retaining state across documents. Attackers controlling an abandoned or subsequent document parsed by a reused parser_for can cause partial string data from one document to appear in another's result.

t: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 Use-After-Free in xmlValidatePopElement
d: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger stale DTD validation states after xmlTextReaderCurrentDoc documents are freed. Attackers can supply an XML document ending with an error inside an element, causing xmlTextReaderClose to read freed element declarations, leading to crashes and possible invalid frees.

t: GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 Double Free in xmlReaderNewWalker()
d: GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a double free vulnerability in xmlReaderNewWalker() that frees reader->input again after xmlTextReaderClose() already released it. Applications reusing a closed xmlTextReader with xmlReaderNewWalker() can crash, and groomed heap memory can control the close callback for possible code execution.

t: libxml2 2.12.6 through 2.15.4 NULL Pointer Dereference via xmlTextReaderConstEncoding()
d: GNOME libxml2 2.12.6 through 2.15.4 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmlTextReaderConstEncoding() after a reader is reset with xmlReaderNewWalker(). Because xmlCtxtReset() leaves ctxt->input NULL, querying the document encoding makes xmlGetActualEncoding() read ctxt->input->flags without a check, crashing the application and causing denial of service.

t: GNOME libxml2 2.14.0 through 2.15.4 Missing NUL Termination in xmlBufferAddHead()
d: GNOME libxml2 2.14.0 through 2.15.4 contains a missing NUL termination flaw in xmlBufferAddHead() in buf.c that leaves uninitialized heap bytes as the terminator for storage-less buffers. Attackers supplying data to applications reusing an xmlBuffer can trigger over-reads via xmlBufferCat() and xmlStrlen(), disclosing adjacent heap memory or causing crashes.

t: FFmpeg through 9.1 Information Disclosure via Frame Buffer Pool Reuse
d: FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because avcodec_flush_buffers() does not release the decoder context's frame buffer pool, so recycled buffers retain prior picture data. Attackers can supply crafted damaged streams to applications reusing one decoder context across users to recover another user's decoded picture content from unwritten frame regions.

t: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via H.264 Encoder Height Change
d: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds write in h264_context_reset() in libfreerdp/codec/h264.c, which stores new dimensions before the YUV planes are reallocated. Remote peers can trigger surface height increases so avc420_compress() writes taller frames past undersized luma and chroma planes, corrupting heap memory or crashing the process.

t: Xiph.Org libvorbis through 1.3.7 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via ov_time_tell
d: Xiph.Org libvorbis through 1.3.7 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ov_time_tell() in lib/vorbisfile.c that reads vf->vi[-1].rate after a failed seek leaves vf->pcm_offset at -1. Attackers can supply a crafted Ogg Vorbis file with a corrupted page to applications that seek and query playback time, leaking heap bytes via the returned value or crashing the process.

t: libvorbis through 1.3.7 Stack Buffer Overflow via _ov_getlap
d: libvorbis through 1.3.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in _ov_getlap() in lib/vorbisfile.c that passes a negative sample count from vorbis_synthesis_lapout() to memcpy(). Attackers can supply a short, valid Ogg Vorbis file with suitable block sizes to overwrite stack frames and crash applications performing two consecutive lapped seeks.

t: libical 4.0.0 before 4.0.7 Infinite Loop via icalrecur_iterator_set_range
d: libical 4.0.0 before 4.0.7 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in icalrecur_iterator_set_range() that allows attackers to cause denial of service by supplying crafted recurrence rules. Attackers can provide a calendar whose recurrence rule is iterated over a reverse range, causing the loop to never terminate and spin the calling thread at full CPU indefinitely.

t: libFLAC 1.5.0 Memory Leak via FLAC__stream_encoder_finish
d: Xiph.Org libFLAC 1.5.0 contains a memory leak in FLAC__stream_encoder_finish() because free_() never releases the main thread task's frame bit writer buffer. Attackers submitting many audio streams to a long-running service that reuses one encoder can leak at least 32 KiB per stream, causing memory exhaustion.

t: GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 NULL Pointer Dereference in xmlParseStartTag2()
d: GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmlParseStartTag2() that allows attackers to crash applications by triggering parser context reuse after SAX1 parsing. Attackers can supply documents with attributes parsed first with XML_PARSE_SAX1 and then without it on a reused context, causing writes to unallocated ctxt->attallocs and denial of service.

t: OpenCV 3.0.0 through 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 MJPEG Encoder Out-of-Bounds Read
d: OpenCV 3.0.0 through 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the built-in MJPEG encoder when writing grayscale frames due to incorrect level shifting in convertToYUV(). Attackers controlling pixel content written as grayscale MJPEG video can trigger unchecked cat_table and huff_dc_tab lookups, leaking adjacent or uninitialized memory into the output file or crashing the process.

t: NodeBB 4.12.0 before 4.16.4 Execution After Redirect via Intents.create
d: NodeBB 4.12.0 before 4.16.4 contains an execution after redirect vulnerability in the Intents.create controller that allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger ActivityPub note ingestion. Attackers can send GET requests to /intents/create with a remote note URI in the toPid parameter to inject federated content as local topics and posts.

t: ProjeQtOr before 13.1.2 Missing Authorization via getAFieldForAClassById.php
d: ProjeQtOr before 13.1.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in tool/getAFieldForAClassById.php that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read any object property. Attackers can request Class=User with an administrator id and field=password or email to retrieve password hashes for offline cracking.

t: Teracom TCW122B-CM before 4.07 Predictable Session Cookie Session Hijacking
d: Teracom TCW122B-CM firmware before 4.07 contains a predictable session cookie vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack administrator sessions by guessing tick-counter-derived cookies. Attackers can predict or brute-force the 32-bit cookie from device uptime and login timing to control relays, settings, and administrator credentials.

t: @irrelon/path 6.2.2 before 7.0.3 Prototype Pollution via merge() and mergeImmutable()
d: @irrelon/path 6.2.2 before 7.0.3 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in merge() and mergeImmutable() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ keys. Attackers can pass untrusted JSON containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype payloads to merged objects, causing property injection, authorization bypass, or denial of service.

t: @oleksii-pavlov/deep-merge before 1.2.4 Prototype Pollution via deepMergeTwoAssignable()
d: @oleksii-pavlov/deep-merge before 1.2.4 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in deepMergeTwoAssignable() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying a __proto__ key. Attackers can pass JSON-parsed input to deepMerge(), deepMergeAndAssign(), deepUpdate() or deepUpdateAndAssign() to inject inherited properties, causing logic bypass or denial of service.

t: merge-deep-composed through 0.1.4 Prototype Pollution via _mergeDeepOne()
d: merge-deep-composed through 0.1.4 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in _mergeDeepOne() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ keys. Attackers can pass JSON-parsed input containing __proto__ as a merge source to inject inherited properties, causing logic bypass or denial of service in Node.js processes.

t: build-git-clone before 1.0.4 OS Command Injection in clone() via repository URL
d: build-git-clone before 1.0.4 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the clone() function that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted repository URLs. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters such as ; or $() in the url argument, which is concatenated into a sh -c command, to execute operating system commands with Node.js process privileges.

t: EverOS before 1.8.0 Cross-Origin Local File Disclosure via Permissive CORS
d: EverOS before 1.8.0 contains a cross-origin local file disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious websites to read local files by abusing a wildcard CORS policy with credentials and unrestricted file:// ingestion. Attackers can host JavaScript that calls POST /api/v2/memory/add with file:// URIs, then read parsed contents via POST /api/v2/memory/search to exfiltrate SSH keys, credentials, and alter or delete memories.

t: Assimp before 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Write via MD5 Importer MakeDataUnique
d: Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::MakeDataUnique() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying unvalidated face indices. Attackers can craft an .md5mesh file with out-of-range face vertex indices or unfilled faces to set bits past the abHad allocation, read vertex data out of bounds, or crash the application.

t: Assimp before 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Write via MD5 Importer LoadMD5MeshFile
d: Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::LoadMD5MeshFile() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via unvalidated weight ranges and bone indices. Attackers can supply a crafted .md5mesh file with out-of-range mBone values to increment heap words past the piCount allocation, causing memory corruption, out-of-bounds reads, or crashes.

t: caoqianming django-vue-admin serializers.py UserModifySerializer dynamically-determined object attributes
d: A security flaw has been discovered in caoqianming django-vue-admin up to 849f9aafa552380c64eecc6059e357f6a1f5437a. This affects the function UserModifySerializer of the file server/apps/system/serializers.py. The manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The patch is identified as d0bc4cf6232798d1f977eb4cad03738a968c4869. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue.

t: OpenEXR: Misaligned pointer store in HTJ2K decoder causes undefined behavior
d: OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. From versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.18 and 3.5.0 through 3.5.2, decoding a crafted HT-compressed EXR chunk can cause ht_undo_impl() to write a 4-byte pixel value through a pointer that is not 4-byte aligned. This happens when the channels sum to a bytes-per-scanline stride that is not a multiple of four. This issue is fixed in versions 3.4.19 and 3.5.3.

t: CodeSafe: safe_eval Sandbox Escape via Indirect Subscript Call
d: CodeSafe is an open-source Python library for code encryption, decryption, and safe evaluation using Python's AST module. From versions 0.0.1 through 0.0.4, the safe_eval() function can be bypassed with indirect subscript calls such as builtins'exec', because AST validation blocks only direct calls to dangerous built-ins. An attacker who controls an expression passed to safe_eval() can execute arbitrary Python code with the permissions of the host application. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.5.

t: Server-Side Request Forgery in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.4 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that on instances with receptive cluster agents enabled could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to make requests to internal network services through the GitLab agent server due to insufficient validation of destination addresses.

t: Incorrect Authorization in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.11 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with developer-role permissions to self-approve their own merge request and merge code into protected branches due to incorrect authorization when a security policy prohibited author self-approval.

t: Session Fixation in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.

t: Incorrect Authorization in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a fine-grained personal access token to read and apply merge request suggestions from projects outside the token's scope due to incorrect authorization checks.

t: Glances: Argument Injection in On-Alert Action Commands via Unescaped Quote Characters in secure.py's Command Tokenizer
d: Glances is an open-source system cross-platform monitoring tool. In versions prior to 4.5.7, the on-alert action command tokenizer in secure.py treats quote characters as argument boundaries without escaping. A monitored stat value, such as a mount point name, that is quoted in an action command template can contain a quote character that breaks out of its quote boundary and injects additional arguments into the process the action invokes. No shell operator is needed for this attack. This issue has been fixed in version 4.5.7.

t: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing server-side input validation on on-call rotation values.

t: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.7 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing resource limits in the error tracking integration.

t: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that on instances with incoming email enabled could have allowed an authenticated user with CI job access to obtain sensitive information belonging to another user due to improper scope validation.

t: Server-Side Request Forgery in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to perform server-side request forgery against internal network resources due to insufficient URL validation in MCP server OAuth handling.

t: Server-Side Request Forgery in GitLab
d: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to send requests to internal network resources due to insufficient validation in repository import.

t: slowlyo owl-admin AdminService.php fillModelFromData dynamically-determined object attributes
d: A vulnerability was identified in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.7. Affected by this issue is the function fillModelFromData of the file src/Services/AdminService.php. The manipulation of the argument id/remember_token/enabled leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.7.8 can resolve this issue. The identifier of the patch is 9b0c98dc3e2710b2ba8d7579da89ec6a4042fcc8. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

t: Munshi Stored HTML Injection via Profile Full Name Field
d: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-15 contained a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to store markup in the profile full_name field by submitting a modified request directly to the backend, which persists the value without sanitization. The Contact Support workflow later inserts the stored name into the generated support email without HTML encoding, so attackers can make injected HTML and media, such as misleading banners, masked hyperlinks and external tracking resources, render in support messages received by the support team.

t: slowlyo owl-admin Admin User Management AdminUserService.php update authorization
d: A vulnerability was detected in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.7. The impacted element is the function update of the file src/Services/AdminUserService.php of the component Admin User Management. The manipulation results in missing authorization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 4.7.8 is sufficient to resolve this issue. The patch is identified as 70910338c1e136d5bdd6ed795768e7a81445f422. The affected component should be upgraded.

t: Munshi Broken Object Level Authorization via invoice/extracted-data Endpoint
d: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a client-supplied extracted_data object without verifying invoice ownership, enforcing the invoice_edit permission or checking whether the invoice has been soft deleted. Authenticated attackers who know an invoice identifier can overwrite seller and buyer details, invoice identifiers, product entries, totals and custom metadata of invoices, including archived invoices marked is_deleted = 1, undermining the integrity of financial records.

t: SeaweedFS S3 API: Bucket policy not enforced on POST Object uploads — an S3 identity can overwrite another identity's data
d: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, the S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on POST Object uploads, which are multipart/form-data POST requests to the bucket. An authenticated S3 identity that a bucket policy restricts, such as to a key prefix or by source IP, can create or overwrite objects it is denied by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT. This issue has been fixed in version 4.46.

t: SeaweedFS: SFTP accepts an empty password for any user account configured without a password (public-key-only users)
d: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, FileStore.ValidatePassword in the SFTP server does not reject zero-length secrets before comparing them, causing an empty login password to match any account configured without one, such as public-key-only or certificate-only users. Because password authentication is enabled by default, a remote attacker who knows a valid username can log in without a key or secret and obtain an SFTP session with that user's home directory and path permissions. This issue is fixed in version 4.46.

t: Camunda 8 Insecure Deserialization via Web Session Storage
d: Camunda 8.8.0 before 8.8.47, 8.9.0 before 8.9.29, 8.10.0 before 8.10.10, and 8.11.0-alpha1 contain an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the persistent web session feature, which stores session attributes as Java-serialized data in secondary storage and deserializes them via an ObjectInputStream without an ObjectInputFilter. Attackers with write access to the web session index, such as an unauthenticated Elasticsearch cluster deployed via Camunda's docker-compose files, can plant a crafted serialized object and trigger deserialization by presenting a matching session cookie, which combined with a gadget chain like the bundled Commons Collections 3.1-RC1 library can lead to code execution as the Camunda service account.

t: vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable vfio_cdx_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set. Userspace can map such a region read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(), writing to MMIO regions the device marks read-only. Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445), drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock: prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable"). Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree cdx device currently publishes a region without the WRITE flag. The guard costs nothing and keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.

t: vfio/fsl-mc: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vfio/fsl-mc: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable vfio_fsl_mc_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set. Userspace can map such a region read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(). Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445), drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock: prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable"). Note this is defensive hardening: the fsl-mc bus publishes all device regions with the WRITE flag set, so no device can currently reach the read-only path. The guard costs nothing and keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.

t: vfio/platform: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vfio/platform: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable vfio_platform_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set. Userspace can map such a region read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(). Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445), drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock: prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable"). Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree platform driver currently publishes a region without the WRITE flag. The guard costs nothing and keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.

t: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Use default TxWindow for zero socket option
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Use default TxWindow for zero socket option L2CAP_OPTIONS accepts a txwin_size of zero and stores it in tx_win. The zero is then sent to the peer in our configuration request, and if the channel ends up in ERTM mode it is passed to l2cap_seq_list_init(). Use the default TxWindow instead, as the mode can still be changed to ERTM during configuration.

t: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject invalid TxWindow in configuration requests
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject invalid TxWindow in configuration requests A peer can send an ERTM RFC option with a TxWindow of zero, which is out of spec. It is stored in remote_tx_win unchanged and later passed to l2cap_seq_list_init(), where roundup_pow_of_two(0) is undefined. On some architectures this results in a ZERO_SIZE_PTR list and a remote kernel oops. A TxWindow above 63 is out of spec as well. With 6-bit sequence numbers we would then send more unacknowledged frames than the sequence space can tell apart. Reply with L2CAP_CONF_UNACCEPT and propose the default TxWindow instead of accepting the value, so remote_tx_win always stays within 1 to 63. Keep the parameters of an earlier request then, and do not treat the request as done because an earlier one was. Also refuse a zero size in l2cap_seq_list_init(), so any other path that reaches it with a zero TxWindow fails the channel instead of the kernel.

t: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject mode changes on connected channels
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject mode changes on connected channels A peer can send a configuration response with an RFC option for another mode to a connected channel, for example to switch it from Streaming to ERTM mode. l2cap_parse_conf_rsp() then changes chan->mode, but l2cap_ertm_init() is not called again, so the ERTM sequence lists are never allocated. The next out-of-sequence I-frame makes l2cap_seq_list_clear() write through the NULL srej_list.list. Refuse the channel when a response tries to change the mode of a connected channel.

t: net: limit priority VLAN untag depth
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: limit priority VLAN untag depth The priority VLAN receive path can repeatedly remove VID 0 tags and retry packet processing. Unlike the read-only VLAN protocol parser, this path has no limit on the number of nested tags it consumes. Each skb_vlan_untag() advances skb->data and resets header offsets. The offsets are stored in 16-bit fields. With enough nested tags, the network or transport offset can wrap. A later protocol handler can then derive a large pull length from the wrapped offsets and access memory outside the skb allocation. Apply the existing VLAN_MAX_DEPTH limit to the exceptional VID 0 retry. Count the tag already stored in skb VLAN metadata as the first level, then stop before untagging a ninth level. Keep the accounting inside this uncommon branch so the regular VLAN receive path is unaffected. A single VID 0 priority tag before a real VLAN tag is valid. No normal deployment was found that intentionally emits multiple consecutive VID 0 tags; permitting eight levels is therefore conservative. The issue was found while researching the Linux network receive path for Google kvmCTF, with OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.6-sol) assisting the analysis. The affected path, reproducer and fix were manually reviewed and tested.

t: slowlyo owl-admin User Management AdminUserService.php saveData authorization
d: A security flaw has been discovered in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.6. This issue affects the function saveData of the file src/Services/AdminUserService.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation of the argument roles results in missing authorization. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 4.7.7 is capable of addressing this issue. The patch is named 762a32a374f68cd2cbad12c0d710dcd537f3b127. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

t: Out-of-bounds read in BSON array decoding in the Python Driver C extension
d: An out-of-bounds read in the native C BSON decoding extension of the MongoDB Python Driver may allow an unauthenticated party who can supply crafted BSON data to the decoder to cause the application process to terminate. In some configurations, nearby process memory may be included in error messages, which may result in limited unintended disclosure of data.

t: Improper certificate revocation check for stapled OCSP responses in the Python Driver
d: An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network endpoint a client connects to, and that holds a revoked but still-dated certificate trusted by that client, to have the connection accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of application credentials and other session data, and in the client treating responses from that endpoint as genuine.

t: Sensitive information in error messages from the Ruby Driver connection string parser
d: An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text of a parsing error, where an existing redaction control does not apply. A party able to read the application's error output or logs may thereby obtain database credential text together with deployment coordinates. The condition arises entirely within the embedding application process and requires no database authentication.

t: Cleartext storage of encrypted embedded fields that use store_as in Mongoid
d: Mongoid builds an incomplete automatic encryption schema for certain embedded document associations. As a result, values that the application declared as encrypted may be written to the database in cleartext, with no error or warning returned to the application. A party holding only basic read privileges on the affected collection, and no access to the encryption keys, may then obtain those values in readable form.

t: Improper restriction of read-only attributes with dotted keys in Mongoid
d: Mongoid does not consistently apply its read-only attribute protection when attribute names are supplied dynamically by the caller. In an application that forwards caller-supplied attribute names into a document update, a user with basic application privileges may change values held inside a field the model declared immutable. This may result in unintended modification of data the application treats as trusted, such as flags used for its own access decisions.

t: Zhengzhou Weiwei Information Technology mayicms member.php sql injection
d: A vulnerability was identified in Zhengzhou Weiwei Information Technology mayicms up to 5.8E. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file member.php. Such manipulation of the argument code leads to sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: Incorrect authorization in has_many delete_all in Mongoid
d: Mongoid contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the handling of caller-supplied filters for bulk removal through a referenced association. Conditions already attached to the association can take precedence over the filter the caller supplied, so records the caller did not select may be removed. A user with basic privileges in an application built on the library may cause unintended removal of records belonging to the same parent record.

t: Cleartext storage of encrypted foreign key fields in Mongoid
d: Mongoid may omit a field from the client-side encryption settings it generates for a collection when that same field is also used as a reference to another record. The value is then stored in readable form instead of encrypted, and the application receives no indication that this has happened. A party with ordinary authenticated read access to the affected collection may be able to view data that was intended to be protected.

t: Incorrect authorization from a discarded default scope in Mongoid
d: A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently discarded when it is combined into a query. A user with basic application privileges who sends an ordinary request may read, change, or remove records that the restriction was intended to withhold.

t: Type confusion in DBPointer handling in BSON Ruby Extended JSON parsing
d: A type-confusion weakness in the Extended JSON parsing component of BSON for Ruby allows a party who can supply parser input to influence how a serialized document is framed. Content placed in one value may be read back as additional or replacement document fields. An unauthenticated party supplying input to an application that parses untrusted Extended JSON and stores the result may cause unintended modification of stored data.

t: Improper restriction of object attributes in Mongoid belongs_to assignment
d: An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a simple identifier value to be turned into an object that is treated as an already-stored record of a caller-chosen model class. In applications that pass unfiltered request data into the affected association handling, an unauthenticated party may cause unintended modification or removal of stored records, and may render an individual record unreadable through that association.

t: Stack-based buffer overflow in mkevent notification mode
d: Stack-based buffer overflow in the mkevent helper in Checkmk <2.5.0p21, <2.4.0p42 and 2.3.0 (EOL) allows an attacker who controls the check output of a monitored host to crash mkevent, causing the notification to be lost, or to redirect the notification to an IPv4 address of their choice, if notifications are forwarded to the Event Console.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Zero-Length LSA Header in ospf.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the LSUpdate.parse function of the NSE ospf.lua library, which does not advance when it reads an LSA header with a zero length. An attacker on the same layer 2 segment can send a single spoofed, unauthenticated OSPF LS Update packet, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process as soon as broadcast-ospf2-discover.nse captures it.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Unbounded Allocation via EIGRP TLV Parser Arithmetic Error in eigrp.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the TLV.AUTH parser of the NSE eigrp.lua library, whose length arithmetic cancels out the running read position. An attacker on the same layer 2 segment can send a single crafted EIGRP Update of roughly 36 bytes over unauthenticated multicast, causing unbounded table growth that exhausts the memory of the Nmap process when broadcast-eigrp-discovery.nse is running.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Scan Freeze via Unreaped Errored Coroutine in tftp.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the dispatcher of the NSE tftp.lua library, which removes completed coroutines but not ones that ended in an error, leaving a zero-yield spin. A malicious TFTP exchange reached by snmp-ios-config.nse after an SNMP write sequence can leave a dead coroutine that freezes the entire Nmap invocation, before port scanning begins for any target in the run; the hang is prevented when the script-timeout option is set.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Malformed Repeat to Address Order in tn3270.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the process_write function of the NSE tn3270.lua library, whose write loop does not advance when it processes a malformed Repeat to Address (RA) order. A malicious TN3270 server on a scanned host can embed a single 6-byte malformed RA order in an ordinary screen-write data stream after a normal negotiation, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process when tn3270-screen.nse runs, which the script-timeout option does not interrupt.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Conformant DEVICETYPE IS Response in tn3270.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the negotiate_tn3270 function of the NSE tn3270.lua library, whose device-type search loop does not advance when the server sends a protocol-conformant DEVICETYPE IS response without an LU suffix. A TN3270E server on a scanned host, including a non-malicious one that sends such a response, causes a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process when tn3270-screen.nse runs, which the script-timeout option does not interrupt.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Memory Exhaustion and Quadratic CPU Use via SOA-over-TCP Response in dns.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the sendPacketsTCP function of the NSE dns.lua library, which reads a DNS-over-TCP response without a size limit and builds it by repeated string concatenation. A malicious DNS server on a scanned host can stream unbounded data in response to the initial SOA lookup made by dns-zone-transfer.nse, before any AXFR request is sent, causing unbounded memory growth and quadratic CPU cost in the Nmap process.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Memory Exhaustion via Uncapped AXFR Read in dns-zone-transfer.nse
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the inline AXFR response reader of the dns-zone-transfer.nse script, which reads the zone transfer response without a size limit. A malicious DNS server on a scanned host can stream unbounded data over TCP port 53 after the AXFR request, causing the memory of the Nmap process to grow at the attacker's send rate until it is exhausted.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Unbounded Allocation via Server-Declared Array Count in msrpctypes.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in the unmarshall_array function of the NSE msrpctypes.lua library, which trusts the entry count declared by the server. A malicious SMB server on a scanned host can declare an EntriesRead value of 0xFFFFFFFF with an empty buffer, causing a prolonged CPU spin and exhausting the memory of the Nmap process; the library is used by smb-enum-shares.nse in the default script category (-sC, -A).

t: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Zero-Length GCC Block in rdp.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the ConfCreateResponse GCC block parser of the NSE rdp.lua library, which does not check that each block advances the read position. A malicious RDP server on a scanned host can include a single malformed zero-length block in an otherwise valid handshake, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process that the script-timeout option does not interrupt; the library is used by rdp-enum-encryption.nse in the default script category (-sC, -A).

t: Nmap < 7.992 Blind Server-Side Request Forgery via Unvalidated UPnP LOCATION URL in broadcast-upnp-info.nse
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the broadcast-upnp-info.nse script and the upnp.lua library, which fetch the device description from the LOCATION URL in a UPnP response without checking that it points to the responding host. An attacker on the local network who answers the script's discovery broadcast can supply a LOCATION URL for an arbitrary host, port and path, including internal and loopback addresses, making Nmap send a GET request there; response content is not returned to the attacker.

t: coleifer peewee File Import pwiz.py _print_table code injection
d: A vulnerability was determined in coleifer peewee up to 4.5.3. This affects the function _print_table of the file pwiz.py of the component File Import Handler. This manipulation causes code injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The reported GitHub issue was closed with the reason "completed". However, it was not possible to determine the PR or commit which could have fixed this issue.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Blind Server-Side Request Forgery via Unvalidated Redirect in http-cisco-anyconnect.nse
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the http-cisco-anyconnect.nse script and the anyconnect.lua library, whose redirect handler follows a server-supplied redirect target without checking that it stays on the scanned host. A malicious web server on a scanned host can redirect Nmap to an arbitrary host and port, including internal and loopback addresses the attacker cannot reach directly, making Nmap send a HEAD request followed by a POST request there; response content is not returned to the attacker. The script runs in the default script category (-sC, -A).

t: Nmap < 7.992 Unbounded Loop via Malicious DRDA Response in drda.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains a loop with an unreachable exit condition in the parameter-list parsing of the NSE drda.lua library, which keeps growing its parameter list while processing a malicious DRDA response. A malicious DRDA service on a scanned host can make the loop consume memory without bound on 64-bit builds, exhausting the Nmap process and discarding NSE results for every other host in the same scan batch without reporting an error; the library is reached by service probes during version detection (-sV).

t: Nmap < 7.992 Cleartext Credential Recovery via Hardcoded DH Exponent in afp.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains a hardcoded cryptographic key vulnerability in the DHCAST128 login of the NSE afp.lua library, which uses a fixed, publicly known Diffie-Hellman private exponent. A passive observer of the network traffic between Nmap and an Apple Filing Protocol server can compute the shared secret from the hardcoded exponent and the server's public value and decrypt the password supplied to scripts such as afp-showmount.nse and afp-brute.nse through the afp.username and afp.password arguments, without man-in-the-middle access or cryptanalysis.

t: Nmap < 7.992 Memory Exhaustion via Unbounded DB2 DAS Packet Length in db2-das-info.nse
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the read_db2_packet function of the db2-das-info.nse script, which trusts an unmasked 32-bit length field supplied by the server. A malicious DB2 Administration Server on a scanned host can declare a packet length of up to roughly 4.29GB, causing the script to buffer that much data and the Nmap process to exhaust memory; the script runs during version detection (-sV).

t: Nmap < 7.992 Memory Exhaustion via Unbounded ONC-RPC Fragment Length in rpc.lua
d: Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the Comm.ReceivePacket function of the NSE rpc.lua library, which buffers ONC-RPC record fragments using the server-declared fragment length without an upper bound. A malicious RPC service on a scanned host can declare fragments of up to roughly 2.1GB, and up to 400 fragments per call, causing the Nmap process to exhaust memory; the read path is reached by rpcinfo.nse during version detection (-sV) and is shared by the NFS, rusers and NetWorker scripts.

t: LibrePhotos ExifTool Metadata Write-Back writer.py write_metadata argument injection
d: A flaw has been found in LibrePhotos up to 1.2.1. Affected by this issue is the function write_metadata of the file apps/backend/api/metadata/writer.py of the component ExifTool Metadata Write-Back. This manipulation of the argument person_name causes argument injection. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.3.0 can resolve this issue. Patch name: f83dafca9f1a6dd0441b7e4d5c13992896a7d76f. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

t: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in Kiro Web
d: Improper sanitization of mixed data and markup elements when processing content in Kiro Web before 2026-10-30, in combination with agents running specific models such as DeepSeek v3.2, GLM-5, MiniMax M2.1, MiniMax M2.5, or Qwen3-coder-next, may allow a remote unauthenticated actor to execute arbitrary commands in a subscriber's hosted development environment via crafted content being repeated back to the user by the agent. AWS has addressed this issue. No customer action is required.

t: Invalid pointer release for non-string option values in the PHP Driver
d: An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Nested View Plugin 241.v178f0b_a_cd76a_ and earlier allows attackers to create views.

Jenkins Configuration as Code Plugin 2134.ve13a_2fc90835 through 2147.v8a_8d38668c72 (both inclusive), except 2140.2142.v3836c98f1b_30, resolves variables, including references to files on the Jenkins controller file system, environment variables, system properties, and values from configured secret sources, in YAML documents submitted to its configuration validation endpoint, and returns resolved values in error responses, allowing attackers with Overall/SystemRead permission to read arbitrary files on the Jenkins controller file system, environment variables, system properties, and values from configured secret sources.
