t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload and File Read via Image Download
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not restrict the source URL, destination path or file type when an unauthenticated AJAX action fetches a file and writes it to a web-accessible directory, allowing unauthenticated users to upload executable PHP files and achieve remote code execution, as well as read arbitrary local files.

t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Page Save
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not restrict the file paths, extensions or contents written by one of its unauthenticated AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to write arbitrary PHP files to a web-accessible directory and execute code on the server.

t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated Image and PDF File Deletion via Path Traversal
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate a user-supplied file path before deleting it, allowing unauthenticated users to delete image and PDF files anywhere the web server can write, including the whole media library.

t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated SSRF
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate URLs taken from the request before fetching them server-side and returning the response, allowing unauthenticated users to make the server request internal resources and read the responses.

t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated SQLi via 'template_id' Parameter
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, allowing unauthenticated users to perform SQL injection attacks.

t: uDraw <= 3.4.0 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via SVG File Upload
d: The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate the type or content of files uploaded through several unauthenticated AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to store SVG files containing JavaScript, which are served from the site's own origin and executed in the browser of any user who opens them, such as an administrator.

t: Addressya <= 3.1.1 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Credentials Settings Update
d: The ADDRESSYA WordPress plugin through 3.1.1 does not have authorisation and CSRF checks when saving its service credentials, and does not escape them when outputting them in an admin page, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators.

t: Synoptic Web Designer <= 1.12 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Administrator via wdh_edit_field_db
d: The Synoptic Web Designer: best WordPress design tool WordPress plugin through 1.12 does not perform any capability, authentication, or nonce check on an action that is also exposed to unauthenticated visitors, and it builds a database UPDATE statement by concatenating unvalidated request input, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite arbitrary database records, including an administrator's password, and take over the site. This is only exploitable on PHP 7.x.
r: Synoptic Web Designer: best WordPress design tool

t: Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce 7.0.0 - 7.3.0 - Unauthenticated Store Data Disclosure and Path Traversal via Print Endpoint
d: The Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0 does not perform authorisation checks when rendering its front-end print document for a reserved order identifier, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the configured store contact details (including the site administrator's email address) and to create Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0 files in arbitrary existing, writable directories outside the Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0's own folder.
r: Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce

t: Tenda RX3 AdvSetMacMtuWan fromAdvSetMacMtuWan command injection
d: A weakness has been identified in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. This affects the function fromAdvSetMacMtuWan of the file /goform/AdvSetMacMtuWan. This manipulation of the argument mac causes command injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

t: Tenda RX3 SetRemoteWebCfg formSetSafeWanWebMan command injection
d: A security flaw has been discovered in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. The impacted element is the function formSetSafeWanWebMan of the file /goform/SetRemoteWebCfg. The manipulation of the argument remoteIp results in command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

t: Tenda RX3 GBK-to-UTF-8 Conversion auto_discover stack-based overflow
d: A vulnerability was identified in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11. The affected element is an unknown function of the file /bin/auto_discover of the component GBK-to-UTF-8 Conversion. The manipulation of the argument Hostname leads to stack-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

t: Tenda RX3 httpd R7WebsSecurityHandler improper authentication
d: A vulnerability was determined in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. Impacted is the function R7WebsSecurityHandler of the component httpd. Executing a manipulation can lead to improper authentication. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

t: partisan decodes peer-plane frames with binary_to_term before authentication, allowing a remote VM abort
d: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way. The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown. This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.

t: Eval injection in Metasploit Framework HWBridge custom method names
d: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection') in the HWBridge custom methods command dispatcher (lib/rex/post/hwbridge/ui/console/command_dispatcher/custom_methods.rb) in Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 on all platforms allows a malicious or compromised hardware bridge to execute arbitrary code in the msfconsole process via a crafted method_name returned by the /custom_methods endpoint. The injected code runs automatically when the operator connects to the bridge, without the operator invoking any custom command.
NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Walrus allows Input Data Manipulation.
Reachable Assertion vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Walrus allows Input Data Manipulation.

t: Rsyslog: rsyslog: omdtls name and fingerprint modes do not verify the dtls server identity
d: A flaw was found in rsyslog. When using the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) output module (omdtls) configured to authenticate receivers by name or fingerprint, the module validates the certificate chain against trusted certificate authorities but fails to verify that the certificate matches the intended receiver's identity or fingerprint. An attacker who can redirect or intercept outbound network traffic and present a certificate issued by a trusted certificate authority could capture forwarded log data, leading to information disclosure.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Improper TLS Certificate Validation via http_download
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in the http_download function of web-lib-funcs.pl that skips TLS chain and hostname verification. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate and substitute downloaded modules, themes, or catalog content, leading to root code execution or injected HTML.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via apache/restart.cgi Error Log Output
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in apache/restart.cgi that displays the last five Apache ErrorLog lines without HTML escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can inject script into error_log via malformed requests or denied paths, executing in a Webmin user's session when Apache fails to restart.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi that allows attackers with LDAP attribute write access to inject markup. Attackers can store script in user or group attributes or the dn, which executes in an administrator's browser when viewing the raw entry.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Improper LDAP Certificate Validation in generic_ldap_connect
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in generic_ldap_connect in ldap-client-lib.pl that accepts any LDAPS or StartTLS server certificate. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the LDAP server to capture the bind DN password, often the root DN, and return forged directory data.

t: Webmin through 2.670 GnuPG Signature Check Bypass in Module Updates
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a signature verification bypass vulnerability in webmin-lib.pl that allows attackers to install unsigned module updates when GnuPG setup fails. Attackers tampering with update downloads via network position or a custom update URL can supply malicious modules that run as root when administrators apply updates.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via mailboxes/detach.cgi Attachment Viewer
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mailboxes/detach.cgi that allows unauthenticated mail senders to bypass the HTML sanitizer. Attackers can send HTML attachments with entity-obfuscated javascript: schemes or encoded script tags in iframe srcdoc to execute script in the Webmin session of users opening them.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via mysql/view_table.cgi Column Names
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/view_table.cgi that allows MySQL users to inject scripts via unescaped column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privilege can create columns containing HTML payloads that execute in a Webmin administrator's session when the table is viewed.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Blocked Users Page
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts by submitting malicious failed-login usernames. Attackers can repeatedly submit crafted usernames until blocked, executing script in administrator sessions viewing edit_blocked.cgi in Webmin or Usermin.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Servers Index Discovery realhost Field
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Servers Index module that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to inject scripts via the realhost field of UDP discovery replies. Attackers on the same broadcast domain can answer discovery scans with HTML or JavaScript stored by find_servers() and rendered unescaped by edit_serv.cgi, executing in Webmin user sessions.

t: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via software/rpmfind.cgi and man/search.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows on-path network attackers to inject script by tampering with plaintext HTTP search results rendered unescaped. Attackers who intercept rpmfind.net or Google responses can inject autofocus/onfocus payloads that execute in a logged-in user's browser within the Webmin origin.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via lpadmin/list_jobs.cgi Print Job Titles
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in lpadmin/list_jobs.cgi that allows local users or network IPP clients to inject script via CUPS print-job titles. Attackers can submit a print job with a crafted title, for example using lp -t, to execute script in a Printer Administration user's Webmin session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Server edit_browser.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-server/edit_browser.cgi that allows attackers with write access to LDAP entry attributes to inject script by storing markup in attribute values. When an administrator browses the entry in the LDAP Server directory browser, the unencoded script runs in the Webmin origin, letting attackers act with the administrator's session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Insecure Upgrade Download via Plaintext HTTP in upgrade.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure download vulnerability in webmin/upgrade.cgi, cluster-webmin/upgrade.cgi and cluster-usermin/upgrade.cgi that fetches upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP with GnuPG signature verification disabled by default. On-path network attackers can substitute a malicious RPM, Debian or tar.gz package during a default upgrade to execute code as root on the Webmin host and managed cluster servers.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Cluster Modules
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying values from managed hosts that cluster modules render unescaped. Attackers who can edit a Servers Index description, control a managed host, or intercept its RPC link can inject server descriptions, versions, user/group names, or package fields to execute JavaScript in the central administrator's session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Perl Code Injection via cluster-useradmin/sync.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a Perl code injection vulnerability in cluster-useradmin/sync.cgi that allows attackers to run code by placing single quotes in home directory paths. Attackers with root on one managed host can craft a home path that breaks out of remote_eval() string literals during Sync, executing Perl as root on other managed hosts.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Upload and Download Module
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Upload and Download module that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped HTTP status lines from background downloads. Attackers controlling a download server can return a malicious status line stored by updown/download.pl and printed unescaped by updown/index.cgi, executing script in a higher-privileged user's session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Client popup_browser.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-client/popup_browser.cgi that allows attackers to inject markup by storing it in LDAP attribute values printed without HTML encoding. Attackers with write access to an LDAP directory entry, needing no Webmin account, can execute scripts in the Webmin origin when an administrator browses that entry.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext LDAP Root DN Password Transmission via ldap-server-lib.pl
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in connect_ldap_db in ldap-server/ldap-server-lib.pl that sends the LDAP root DN password unencrypted when encryption is set to Detect automatically. Passive network attackers observing traffic between Webmin and a remote LDAP server can capture directory root credentials because the connection loop always reaches a plaintext bind attempt.

t: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via status/edit_mon.cgi Monitor Descriptions
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in status/edit_mon.cgi that allows attackers to inject scripts through unescaped monitor status descriptions. Malicious HTTP or FTPS server operators, on-path attackers, or local users creating crafted filenames in wildcard-monitored directories can execute JavaScript in a Webmin user's session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Predictable Password Generation in Users and Groups Module
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak random password generation vulnerability in generate_random_password() that allows attackers to predict generated account passwords because seed_random() effectively seeds Perl rand() with only time XOR process ID. When the non-default random_password option is enabled and administrators keep the pre-filled password in edit_user.cgi, attackers can enumerate time and PID seeds to recover passwords and authenticate as new accounts.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Mail Queue Attachment Filenames
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in postfix/view_mailq.cgi and sendmail/view_mailq.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via unsanitized MIME attachment filenames. Attackers can send a message with a crafted Content-Disposition or Content-Type filename that remains queued, executing script in the Webmin session of users viewing it.

t: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via mount/nfs_export.cgi NFS Export Chooser
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mount/nfs_export.cgi that allows malicious NFS servers to inject scripts through unescaped export paths. Attackers controlling or spoofing an NFS server's mountd replies can return crafted export paths that execute JavaScript in the session of a Webmin user browsing exports.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation in switch_smtp_to_ssl
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in switch_smtp_to_ssl in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl and status/smtp-monitor.pl, which calls Net::SSLeay::connect without certificate verification or a hostname check. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate when SMTP with SSL or STARTTLS is configured to capture SMTP AUTH credentials and message content.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via User and Group Chooser Popups
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows local users or directory writers to inject script by placing markup in user names, group names or GECOS fields. Attackers can set GECOS via chfn or modify LDAP, NIS or SSSD entries so unescaped values in my_user_chooser.cgi, my_group_chooser.cgi, user_chooser.cgi and group_chooser.cgi execute in a Webmin user's browser.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via quota/list_users.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Disk Quotas module that allows directory administrators to inject markup via NSS user names. Attackers who can create or rename LDAP, NIS or SSSD identities owning blocks on XFS quota filesystems can execute script in the browser of administrators viewing quota/list_users.cgi.

t: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via MySQL Module mysql/index.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/index.cgi that renders MySQL connection error text and server version strings without escaping. Malicious MySQL server operators or on-path attackers on plaintext connections can return markup in error packets or version strings to execute JavaScript in Webmin user sessions.

t: Webmin through 2.670 RCE via Plaintext CPAN Downloads in Perl Modules
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Perl Modules (cpan) module, which downloads CPAN indexes and module archives over plaintext HTTP without checksum or signature verification. On-path network attackers can answer the outbound fetch while an administrator installs a CPAN module, supplying a malicious Makefile.PL that cpan/download.cgi runs as root before confirmation.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Samba Attributes in edit_user.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/edit_user.cgi that allows attackers to inject markup through the LDAP sambaAcctFlags and sambaBadPasswordCount attributes, which are rendered without HTML encoding. Attackers with LDAP write access to these attributes can store malicious scripts that execute in a Webmin administrator's browser when the user entry is opened in the editor.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation in servers/save_serv.cgi Fast-RPC Probe
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that allows man-in-the-middle attackers to capture credentials because servers/save_serv.cgi skips the selected SSL certificate check. When fast RPC is set to Automatic, attackers intercepting the /fastrpc.cgi probe can obtain the remote Webmin username and password sent via HTTP Basic Authorization.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via init/mass_systemd.cgi Journal Output
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in init/mass_systemd.cgi that prints unescaped journalctl output when a systemd service fails to start. Attackers can inject script into the journal via logger or sshd invalid user names, executing it in an administrator's Webmin session.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation via servers/link.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in servers/link.cgi that accepts self-signed certificates for linked servers even when certificate checking is enabled. Man-in-the-middle attackers presenting a self-signed certificate with the correct hostname can capture stored HTTP Basic credentials for the remote Webmin and inject HTML into the local Webmin origin.

t: Webmin through 2.670 OS Command Injection via ldap-client/check.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in ldap-client/check.cgi that allows LDAP directory writers to execute commands via unquoted uid values. Attackers can create a posixAccount entry with shell metacharacters in its uid, executing commands as root when an administrator runs Check Configuration.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Predictable TOTP Secret Generation via generate_base32_secret()
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak randomness vulnerability that allows attackers to predict TOTP two-factor secrets generated by generate_base32_secret() using a time and PID seeded rand(). Attackers who know a user's password and estimate enrollment time can enumerate candidate seeds, reproduce the secret, and bypass the second authentication factor.

t: Webmin through 2.670 STARTTLS Downgrade via send_mail in boxes-lib.pl
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a STARTTLS downgrade vulnerability in send_mail in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl that continues over plaintext when STARTTLS is rejected. Man-in-the-middle attackers can strip or reject STARTTLS to capture configured SMTP AUTH credentials, crackable CRAM-MD5 exchanges, and the content of sent mail.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Insecure Usermin Upgrade Download via upgrade.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing integrity verification vulnerability in usermin/upgrade.cgi that downloads Usermin upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP without signature or digest checks. On-path network attackers or DNS spoofers can supply a malicious RPM, Debian, or tar.gz package whose maintainer scripts or setup.sh execute as root during upgrade.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Default Admin Credentials via Windows setup.bat
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure default configuration in its Windows setup.bat script that provisions an administrator account with the credentials admin/admin and SSL disabled. Unauthenticated network attackers can log in over plain HTTP on port 10000 with these unchanged credentials to gain full Webmin administrative access.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Missing IMAP Certificate Validation in imap_login
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in imap_login in mailboxes/folders-lib.pl that skips certificate verification and hostname checks for IMAP SSL connections. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate to capture IMAP credentials sent by the System and Server Status IMAP monitor and spoof monitor results.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Minecraft save_backup.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in minecraft/save_backup.cgi that allows local attackers with write access to the Minecraft server directory to inject script via unescaped world directory names. Attackers can create a world directory containing HTML or script that executes in a Webmin user's session when they run Backup Now.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Missing Authentication on fastrpc.cgi File-Transfer Sockets
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in fastrpc.cgi that allows unauthenticated network peers to connect to tcpwrite and tcpread file-transfer listeners without session checks. Attackers can race to connect to the predictable transfer port during cluster operations to steal transferred files or replace staged packages, achieving root code execution.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Authentication Bypass via password_change.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in password_change.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to change passwords for accounts with empty stored hashes. When passwd_mode is 2, attackers can POST user, old, new1 and new2 with any old value to set a known password and gain access.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Path Traversal via Minecraft Server Playtime Limits
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a path traversal vulnerability in minecraft/minecraft-lib.pl that allows unauthenticated game players to overwrite arbitrary files as root via crafted chat messages. Attackers can send chat messages mimicking logged in lines so the root check_playtime_limits cron job rewrites attacker-chosen files, destroying their contents.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via proc/trace.cgi Running Processes Trace
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in proc/trace.cgi that allows local unprivileged OS users to inject markup via unescaped process arguments and system call parameters. Attackers can craft process command lines or file names passed to open so that script executes in a Webmin user's session when they trace the process.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext Credential Transmission via status/smtp-monitor.pl
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in the SMTP service monitor that never issues STARTTLS because get_smtp_status tests an undefined $ssl variable. Passive network attackers can capture AUTH PLAIN credentials sent in plaintext each time a STARTTLS-configured monitor runs, without needing a Webmin login.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext Transmission of Fast RPC Traffic via fastrpc.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in web-lib-funcs.pl and fastrpc.cgi that sends cluster RPC traffic over raw TCP despite SSL configuration. Network-positioned attackers can read the session ID and remote_eval payloads or alter calls in transit to execute code as root on managed servers.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Header Directive Injection via sendmail/autoreply.pl
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a header directive injection vulnerability in sendmail/autoreply.pl that allows unauthenticated mail senders to inject autoreply directives by placing them in inbound subject, from, date, or body fields. Attackers can inject Reply-Tracking to delete files at chosen paths, Autoreply-File to exfiltrate files readable by the delivery user, or arbitrary reply headers including To.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via logrotate/force.cgi
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in logrotate/force.cgi that prints logrotate -f diagnostic output without HTML escaping. Local OS users can create files with script-laden names in wildcard-rotated log directories, executing script in the Webmin session when Force Log Rotation is clicked.

t: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via useradmin/edit_user.cgi Home Directory
d: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in useradmin/edit_user.cgi that displays home directory paths without HTML escaping to users with the autohome ACL. A Webmin user with broader Users and Groups rights can store a home path containing script via save_user.cgi, executing it in a restricted sub-administrator's Webmin session.

t: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory Vulnerability in Cosminexus Component Container
d: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory Vulnerability in Cosminexus Component Container. This issue affects Cosminexus Component Container: from 11-20 before 11-70-04.

t: Keycloak-operator: keycloak-operator: secret-derived hashes exposed in statefulset metadata and keycloakoidcclient status
d: A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

t: league/commonmark 2.6.0 before 2.10.8 Denial of Service via max_delimiters_per_line Bypass
d: league/commonmark 2.6.0 before 2.10.8 contains a denial of service vulnerability in DelimiterStack::push() that miscounts delimiter runs against the max_delimiters_per_line budget. Attackers submitting Markdown with two long emphasis character runs can produce deeply nested strong elements, causing quadratic rendering time and CPU exhaustion.

t: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 Out-of-Bounds Read via Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength
d: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength in src/avtp/acf/custom/Vss.c, which reads the INTEROP path-length prefix without checking the declared ACF message length. Attackers can send header-only 12-byte INTEROP-mode VSS frames to trigger reads past the buffer, or prefix values 0xFFFE and 0xFFFF that wrap uint16 lengths and cause Avtp_Vss_SetVssData to overwrite the path area.

t: Shopify async-memcached before 0.11.0 Meta Protocol Injection via Meta Flags
d: Shopify async-memcached before 0.11.0 contains a command injection vulnerability in Client::validate_meta_flags that allows attackers to inject extra memcached meta protocol tokens via whitespace in flags. Attackers controlling part of a meta flag can add quiet, opaque, mode or size override tokens to alter operations and desynchronize responses on shared connections.

t: Karakeep before 0.35.0 Improper Access Control via lists.merge Procedure
d: Karakeep before 0.35.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability in ManualList.mergeInto that allows list owners to retain collaborator bookmarks by merging shared lists without ownership checks. Owners invoking the lists.merge tRPC procedure create rows not tied to collaborator membership, preserving read access to collaborator bookmarks and assets after the collaborator's access is revoked.

t: Karakeep before 0.35.0 Information Disclosure via Shared-List Bookmark Filters
d: Karakeep before 0.35.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows shared-list collaborators to learn other users' private favourited and archived bookmark state through filter queries. Viewer or editor collaborators can call bookmarks.getBookmarks on a shared list with favourited or archived set to true, inferring owners' private flags from which bookmarks buildCommonFilters returns.

t: pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 Arbitrary File Write via commit_payment_batch
d: pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the commit_payment_batch MCP tool that allows attackers to write files outside any output directory via output_file_path. Attackers can stage a batch, reuse the self-issued confirmation_token, and supply absolute, dot-dot, or symlinked paths to create or overwrite server-writable files with generated XML.

t: LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 STEP Record Injection
d: LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 contain a STEP record injection vulnerability in the mutation writer via unescaped typed-value type names. Attackers controlling the mutations payload can place parentheses, semicolons, and newlines in typed.type to append arbitrary entity records to exported IFC files, bypassing the class-name guard.

t: WeKan before 12.78 Information Disclosure via Board Export checklistId Parameter
d: WeKan before 12.78 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in Exporter.buildStream() that lets attackers retrieve checklists from other boards by supplying a checklistId export scope. Users able to export any board, or unauthenticated users via a public board, can read private checklists, their items and creator usernames even when anonymization is enabled.

t: WeKan before 12.78 Export Restriction Bypass via Streaming CSV/TSV Export
d: WeKan before 12.78 contains an access control bypass in Exporter.buildCsvStream() that ignores the Disable all export and Anonymize export users settings. Board readers or unauthenticated users of public boards can request the CSV export endpoint to export all cards and reveal real usernames in member, assignee, and mention fields.

t: lightNVR before 0.44.3 Authorization Bypass via go2rtc Proxy src Parameter
d: lightNVR before 0.44.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in go2rtc_proxy_authorize_request() that allows authenticated users to access restricted cameras by exploiting inconsistent src parameter parsing. Attackers can percent-encode a second src parameter name or exceed the 255-byte truncation so go2rtc resolves a different camera, obtaining unauthorized snapshots and HLS live streams.

t: ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 Symlink Arbitrary File Overwrite via ai-memory-wikisync
d: ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. Attackers can place a .wikisync-tmp-<page>.md symlink in a shared destination so atomic_write() truncates and overwrites its target with the victim's privileges.

t: SRS before 6.0.194, 7.0.214, and 8.0.73 Heap Buffer Overflow via RTCP Decoding
d: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.

t: SRS before 6.0.194, 7.0.214, and 8.0.73 Reachable Assertion via RTCP Length
d: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a reachable assertion in RTCP decoding that lets remote WebRTC peers crash the server. Attackers opening an unauthenticated WHIP or WHEP session can send an 8-byte RTCP packet with undersized length, triggering srs_assert aborts that stop every stream.

t: Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux Origin Validation Error via IPC Bridge
d: Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux contains an origin validation error in the sendMessageToBackend WebKitGTK handler that allows child-frame scripts to invoke the privileged IPC channel. Attackers controlling content loaded in an iframe can post messages that pass the top-level URI origin check and call bound Go methods and Wails runtime operations.

t: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 .actrc Allowlist Bypass via Argument Smuggling
d: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.

t: Electerm before 5.9.0 RCE via DNS Rebinding in MCP Server Widget
d: Electerm before 5.9.0 contains an origin validation vulnerability in the MCP Server widget that allows remote attackers to execute commands by bypassing Host and Origin checks through DNS rebinding. Attackers can lure users to a page that rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and calls unauthenticated MCP tools on port 30837 to run OS commands locally and on open SSH sessions.

t: Mastodon 4.7.4 and 4.8.0-alpha.3 before 5.0.0-beta.1 Authentication Bypass via Sign-In Token
d: Mastodon 4.7.4 and 4.8.0-alpha.3 before 5.0.0-beta.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in authenticate_with_sign_in_token that allows authenticated local users to rebind pending login attempts to other accounts. Attackers can submit sign_in_token_resend with a victim's user[email] parameter, then guess the unthrottled 6-character token to sign in as inactive accounts lacking two-factor authentication.

t: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.1, 17.7.3, 17.8.2, 17.9.7 Arbitrary Method Invocation
d: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection vulnerability in InplaceEditFieldsController via the unvalidated attribute parameter. Users who can view a project can request the inplace_edit_fields reset route with attribute destroy to delete projects and subprojects, or invoke other methods exposing restricted data.

t: nliautaud pico-content-editor Authorization Uploads.php init unrestricted upload
d: A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Uploads::saveFile/Auth::init of the file src/Uploads.php of the component Authorization Subsystem. Such manipulation of the argument PicoContentEditorUpload leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

t: browser-use SecurityWatchdog config.py load_and_migrate_config improper authorization
d: A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

t: Rsyslog: rsyslog: improper json escaping in option.json="on" template path for quote-only and backslash-only values
d: A flaw was found in rsyslog. When processing log entries using certain JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) formatting templates, the service fails to properly escape input composed entirely of quotation marks or backslashes. An attacker who can supply logged input can exploit this issue to generate malformed JSON output, which may cause downstream log ingestion systems and parsers to reject log records.

t: Rsyslog: rsyslog: imuxsock buffer underwrite in pid rewriting
d: A flaw was found in rsyslog. When process identification (PID) rewriting is enabled in the imuxsock module, a local attacker with access to the logging socket can send a crafted log message with an empty tag. This triggers an invalid memory write, causing the logging service to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

t: JaguarJack catch-admin RolesController.php update dynamically-determined object attributes
d: A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. This affects the function update of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. The manipulation leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

t: Qemu-kvm: qemu-kvm: guest-triggerable host heap over-read via vhost vring unmap after queue size change
d: A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software. A privileged user inside a guest virtual machine could use this flaw to make the host QEMU process copy parts of its own memory into the guest's memory, where the attacker could read it. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to view portions of the host QEMU process memory from within a guest, potentially exposing sensitive information that could aid in further attacks. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

t: Kubevirt: containerized-data-importer: cdi: upload client certificate identity injection via uploadclientname pvc annotation enables cross-namespace writes
d: A flaw was found in kubevirt Containerized Data Importer (CDI). The CDI clone controller derives the CommonName of a CDI-CA-signed upload client certificate from the tenant-settable cdi.kubevirt.io/uploadClientName PVC annotation without validation, and the upload server authenticates clients only by certificate CA chain and CommonName string match, with no namespace or PVC binding. A namespace user can obtain a valid client certificate and write arbitrary data into any upload-ready PVC in any namespace whose upload Service is reachable from the cluster network, resulting in cross-namespace integrity impact on disk images used by virtual machines.

t: Gst-plugins-bad: gst-plugins-bad: mxfdemux out-of-bounds read via unvalidated signed index-table-segment fields
d: A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-bad mxfdemux handling of MXF Index Table Segment data. Crafted index metadata can lead to an out-of-range lookup during a seek and terminate the media process. A Fedora 43 test reproduced an assertion-triggered abort. The upstream advisory also notes possible information disclosure, but an attacker-visible leak has not been demonstrated.

t: JaguarJack catch-admin RolesController.php store dynamically-determined object attributes
d: A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The impacted element is the function store of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

t: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: policy-selected otp flow accepts password sso
d: A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.

t: Akaunting 3.3.0 - Stored cross-site scripting through imported tax names in update notifications
d: Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the XLSX tax-import workflow. An authenticated Manager can import HTML in a tax name and associate the tax with an item. When an Administrator attempts to disable that tax, Akaunting renders the original stored name in an error notification through Vue v-html, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute within the browser of another authenticated user.

t: JaguarJack catch-admin User Management UserController.php Update dynamically-determined object attributes
d: A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

t: AutoGPT: Template rendering was not bounded in size or time
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.11.0, template rendering is not bounded in size or time. Any signed-up user who can reach a block that takes a format string, such as Fill Text Template or Agent Output, through POST /api/blocks/{id}/execute or the external API's block-execute route, can make the REST API process allocate without bound with one request of a few dozen bytes. This can stop the process from answering any request, including its health check. There is no data read or change impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: Dynamically priced blocks bypass credit billing and balance checks when cost-determining inputs are left unset
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.3.4 before 0.11.0, LLM and other dynamically priced blocks run without charge when a priced input is left at its schema default. An account with a credit balance of zero can make unlimited language-model, code-generation, and image-generation calls at the operator's expense while the platform records the usage at zero cost. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: DWS Antik Browser Local API Server index.ts origin validation
d: A weakness has been identified in DWS Antik Browser 1.17.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file src/server/index.ts of the component Local API Server. Executing a manipulation can lead to origin validation error. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones
d: Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones. The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24. An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

t: vanna-ai vanna FAISS AgentMemory Integration agent_memory.py _load_index deserialization
d: A security flaw has been discovered in vanna-ai vanna 2.0.0/2.0.1/2.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is the function _load_index of the file src/vanna/integrations/faiss/agent_memory.py of the component FAISS AgentMemory Integration. Performing a manipulation results in deserialization. The attack needs to be approached locally. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: GV-EBD4700 Series Default HTTPS private key
d: An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at /program/www/ssl_cert.pem and copied to /config/ssl_cert.pem during initialization. When HTTPS is enabled using the default certificate, a network on-path attacker who obtains the firmware image can use the exposed private key to present an identical certificate and intercept HTTPS traffic. HTTPS is disabled by default . * Only impacts deployments where an administrator enables HTTPS and retains the default certificate. Because the private key is publicly distributed in the firmware image, an on-path attacker can impersonate the device with an identical certificate fingerprint, bypassing fingerprint checks and stored certificate exceptions (potentially capturing credentials if a user clicks through the expired-certificate warning).

t: AutoGPT Platform: E2B code-execution blocks leave sandboxes running on the operator's shared credential beyond the billed runtime
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.4.2 before 0.11.0, the E2B code-execution blocks ExecuteCodeBlock, InstantiateCodeSandboxBlock, and ClaudeCodeBlock can leave sandboxes running on the operator's shared E2B credential for up to the sandbox's full timeout, while users are billed only for the block's run time. Any user with a positive credit balance can keep sandboxes running for up to 24 hours on a Pro plan for a flat 1 credit, and each run adds another sandbox. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: AutoGPT: Denial of service via unbounded `format` Jinja filter width in TextFormatter (un-patched sibling of CVE-2026-33235)
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.10.0, the format Jinja filter in TextFormatter accepts an unbounded width. An authenticated user who can author or run a workflow, or supply its input, can trigger a single synchronous multi-gigabyte allocation that exhausts the executor worker's memory and degrades or denies execution for other users. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

t: AutoGPT: Open Redirect in OAuth authorize endpoint via unvalidated error redirects
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.10.0, the OAuth authorize endpoint redirects to unvalidated error redirect targets. An attacker can craft a link on the platform's own domain that redirects a signed-in user to an attacker-controlled site, which can present a lookalike consent or sign-in page to harvest credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

t: Backdrop CMS Views views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc get_argument authorization
d: A vulnerability was identified in Backdrop CMS up to 1.35.2. Affected is the function get_argument of the file core/modules/views/plugins/views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc of the component Views Module. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The config-import path enforces no 'use PHP for settings' check while the Views PHP-code argument plugin executes eval() without a permission check, confirming the authorization bypass. The vendor explains: "As per our security advisory policy, no security advisory is required when an exploit requires 'advanced permissions'."

t: Out-of-bounds read in the PSA ECDSA signature DER parser on a malformed signature TLV before verification
d: MCUboot's PSA-crypto ECDSA adapter parses the RFC 5480 DER signature with parse_signature_from_rfc5480_encoding() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/ecdsa.h, which takes no length argument. bootutil_ecdsa_verify() explicitly discards the signature length ((void)slen;) and the parser walks the encoding using length bytes read from the buffer itself (r_len = sig[3], then a derived s_len), with no check that those offsets stay within the supplied signature. Because this parsing runs before psa_verify_hash(), a malformed signature triggers the read whether or not the signature is valid. In bootutil_img_validate() (boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c:404) the ECDSA signature TLV is gated only by len > sizeof(buf), since EXPECTED_SIG_LEN() is the constant 1 for ECDSA; len is attacker-controlled in the range 0..128 and is copied into the 128-byte stack buffer buf. With a crafted r_len (e.g. sig[3] = 255) the parser's memcpy reads roughly 130+ bytes past the end of buf, an out-of-bounds read of adjacent stack memory. Reaching the signature case only requires a key TLV that matches a trusted public key (public material), so the path is effectively pre-authentication. The defect is gated to the PSA crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_PSA_CRYPTO) with MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC256/MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384 (and MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384 always builds with PSA); the in-tree CC310, TinyCrypt, and mbedTLS adapters use different decoders and are not affected. This is not a signature bypass: the over-read bytes feed a verification that fails closed and are never returned to the attacker, so there is no information leak. The impact is bounded to a possible fault/denial-of-service on memory layouts where the read crosses an unmapped region; on typical flat-memory MCUs it reads adjacent RAM without faulting. This vulnerability was reported independently twice: by NVIDIA Project Vanessa on 2026-06-22, and by Kai Phan (@kaimandalic) on 2026-07-19 as GHSA-r44p-8v6p-hqv4, which is closed as a duplicate of this advisory. Both original reports are reproduced in full below. The second report additionally observes that bootutil_ecdsa_parse_public_key() discards its end pointer ((void)end;, ecdsa.h:446). That observation is correct, but it is not part of this vulnerability and is not counted in the severity: the buffer it parses is bootutil_keys[key_id].key, the compiled-in trusted key store (image_ecdsa.c:54-55), so no attacker-controlled data reaches that parse. It is a robustness gap on the same code path and should be closed alongside the signature-parser fix. Note also that the second report's proof-of-concept models the signature buffer as an 8-byte heap allocation and therefore reports a heap overflow; in MCUboot the buffer is the 128-byte stack array buf, gated by len > sizeof(buf), so the real over-read is of adjacent stack memory.

t: Espressif flash-encryption provisioning leaves eFuse key material and plaintext sector buffers on the bootloader stack
d: MCUboot's Espressif port omits zeroization of two sensitive stack buffers in boot/espressif/hal/src/flash_encrypt.c. In check_and_generate_encryption_keys(), the freshly generated XTS-AES flash-encryption key is held in the stack array keys[BLOCKS_NEEDED][32] (flash_encrypt.c:216), written to eFuse via esp_efuse_write_keys(), and the function returns (flash_encrypt.c:243) without scrubbing it. In esp_flash_encrypt_region(), the plaintext flash sector buffer buf (flash_encrypt.c:454) retains the last sector's cleartext at both the success and flash_failed returns. Neither path performs a memset/bzero/mbedtls_platform_zeroize, even though the same port already does bzero for key digests in boot/espressif/hal/src/secure_boot.c. The affected code runs only on the Espressif port with CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, and only during the one-time first-boot provisioning pass when flash encryption is not yet enabled (boot/espressif/main.c); on subsequent boots the buffers are never created. Recovering the residue requires an out-of-band stack/RAM-disclosure primitive — JTAG/debug halt, UART ROM download, a core/crash dump, or a warm-boot RAM scrape — captured during that single provisioning boot. Under the recommended CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_RELEASE plus secure boot, those channels are fused off and no exposure exists. The practical impact is a low-severity, defense-in-depth hardening gap: a flash-encryption key (and last plaintext sector) may linger in bootloader stack memory. Because the eFuse key block is burned read+write-protected, the transient stack copy is the only readable copy, and only during one boot; in a development build where a disclosure channel is open, an attacker with that capability can usually already read the still-plaintext flash directly, so the marginal confidentiality gain is small. Confirming real-world recovery depends on a specific SoC/debug configuration not exercisable from source alone.

t: Cypress/PSoC6 flash backend fails to bounds-check flash accesses, allowing pre-auth out-of-bounds reads
d: The Cypress/PSoC6 flash-map backend in boot/cypress/cy_flash_pal/cy_flash_map.c guards every flash access with assert() against the wrong struct field. flash_area_read(), flash_area_write(), and flash_area_erase() check assert(off < fa->fa_off) and assert(off + len < fa->fa_off), comparing the area-relative off against the partition's absolute base address fa->fa_off instead of its length fa->fa_size. Because fa_off is a large absolute address, realistic out-of-partition offsets pass the check even in a debug build, and under NDEBUG the asserts are removed entirely. The access then proceeds as memcpy() (or a flash row op) at fa->fa_off + off with no enforcement. The MCUboot core does not bound image-region offsets itself; it relies on flash_area_read() returning an error. During pre-authentication image validation, bootutil_img_hash() in boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_img_hash.c loops over ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size + ih_protect_tlv_size — all attacker-controlled header fields of the still-unverified update image — calling flash_area_read(), and the TLV iterator in boot/bootutil/src/tlv.c reads attacker-derived offsets the same way. An attacker who can stage a crafted image in the secondary/update slot (via OTA, DFU, or serial recovery, depending on the product) declares an oversized ih_img_size, causing reads far past the partition. A correct backend would reject these and fail validation cleanly; the Cypress backend does not. The out-of-bounds access is in the source address of the copy — the destination buffer is correctly sized — so there is no memory corruption, no information disclosure to the attacker (the data is only folded into a hash that still fails the signature check), and no authentication bypass. The realistic impact is a bus fault or hang when the computed absolute address lands on an unmapped or peripheral region of the PSoC6 address map: the bootloader crashes instead of rejecting the bad image, an availability (denial-of-service) impact. The defect is specific to the Cypress/PSoC6 port; mainline Zephyr/sim/mynewt backends are unaffected. The identical broken guard in the write/erase primitives is a latent out-of-bounds-write gap, but no attacker-controlled out-of-bounds offset was found to reach those (serial-recovery uploads are bounded by the core), so the reachable memory-safety bug is the out-of-bounds read.

t: MCUboot swap resume trusts a flash-resident swap_size, allowing pre-authentication out-of-bounds flash operations
d: When MCUboot resumes an interrupted image swap it takes the number of bytes to move straight from the flash-resident status trailer. In boot_swap_image() (boot/bootutil/src/loader.c) the fresh-swap branch recomputes copy_size from the image headers and is bounded — swap_run() in boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c carries an explicit "not enough free space" check (last_idx >= first_trailer_idx) — but that check runs only inside if (boot_status_is_reset(bs)). On the resume branch the code instead does boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); copy_size = bs->swap_size; and passes the value to swap_run() with no re-derivation and no bound. swap_run() turns that byte count into a sector index by summing sector sizes until it reaches the count, with no ceiling on the real sector count: find_last_idx() in swap_move.c and swap_offset.c, and find_last_sector_idx() in swap_scratch.c, are all while (1) loops. The resulting index is fed to boot_img_sector_off() / boot_img_sector_size() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_priv.h), which index the fixed BOOT_MAX_IMG_SECTORS sectors[] arrays with no bounds check. Past num_sectors the loop reads zero-initialised — and past BOOT_MAX_IMG_SECTORS, adjacent-struct — entries; a sector size of 0 makes the loop never terminate, and a bogus computed offset is handed to boot_erase_region() / boot_copy_region() as an out-of-bounds flash erase or copy. MCUboot itself only ever writes a validated, slot-bounded swap_size (swap_misc.c, fixup_revert()), so reaching the defect requires writing the trailer from outside. Serial recovery provides exactly that: an upload writes attacker bytes contiguously from offset 0 of the primary slot (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c, via flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot()), bounded only by img_size <= area_size, so it controls the whole trailer — magic, swap_info, op/idx/state and swap_size. The resume gate boot_status_is_reset() keys solely on those op/idx/state fields, and boot_find_status() explicitly trusts valid magic as implying valid metadata. A forged in-progress status with an oversized swap_size therefore drives the unbounded walk during swap setup — before the primary image's signature is validated, and serial recovery is unauthenticated by design. The outcome is an out-of-bounds flash erase or copy, or a non-terminating loop, inside the bootloader: an unbootable or bricked device, with the possibility of bootloader memory corruption. That exceeds what serial recovery is designed to grant, which is only the ability to stage an image that must still pass signature verification. Exposure requires a swap-based update backend — MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_MOVE (the default for swap builds), MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_SCRATCH or MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_OFFSET; overwrite-only, direct-XIP and RAM-load builds are unaffected — together with MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY. Without serial recovery the path is only reachable by an attacker who can already write flash directly, which is outside the threat model. The fix is to treat the trailer's swap_size as untrusted: reject or clamp it in boot_swap_image() before it becomes copy_size, bounding it by the primary slot's usable image area (sector count x sector size, excluding the trailer) rather than the raw flash_area_get_size(), and aborting recovery with a non-zero error on overflow. The same guard should cover the independent boot_read_swap_size() reads in each backend's boot_read_image_header().

t: Zefan-Cai R-KV FlashInfer weight loader loader.py _shard_files path traversal
d: A vulnerability was determined in Zefan-Cai R-KV up to 6715468b9872442be72e5c97322e4d9c9a2abf55. This impacts the function _shard_files of the file FlashInfer/rkv/loader.py of the component FlashInfer weight loader. This manipulation of the argument weight_map causes path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. Patch name: 0fdff6ed12b58ad4c33aab5a63f66e04555cafb6. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

t: AutoGPT Platform Backend: MCPToolBlock Auto-Lookup Lets a Shared Agent's Author Use the Runner's MCP Credentials
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.6.49 before 0.11.0, the MCPToolBlock auto-lookup allows a shared agent's author to use the MCP credentials of the user who runs it. Anyone who ran a shared agent containing an MCPToolBlock node, and had already connected the MCP server URL that the node names, had that connection used for any read, write, or delete the server exposes, with the result sent to a host chosen by the author. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: AutoGPT: Office preview expands an unbounded embedded ZIP thumbnail
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.6.63 before 0.11.0, the Office preview expands an embedded ZIP thumbnail without a size limit. A signed-in user with access to workspace file previews can exhaust the memory of a platform API worker with one small crafted DOCX, XLSX, or PPTX file and one preview request. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: Netis WF2409E CGI skk_set.cgi improper authentication

t: AutoGPT: Host-scoped credential headers leaked to other hosts through HTTP redirects
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.15 through 0.10.0, the value of a host-scoped credential header was exposed to other hosts via HTTP redirects. SendAuthenticatedWebRequestBlock attaches a host-scoped credential's headers to a request, but once a redirect took that request to a different origin, only three fixed header names (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) were removed. A host-scoped credential's header names are free-form (the UI suggests X-API-Key), so a credential carried under any other name followed the redirect to the new origin. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: Unbounded CBOR recursion in MCUboot serial recovery allows pre-authentication stack exhaustion
d: The vendored zcbor decoder's zcbor_any_skip() in boot/zcbor/src/zcbor_decode.c descends one C-stack frame per level of CBOR nesting. On a list or map it copies the decoder state (memcpy(&state_copy, state, sizeof(zcbor_state_t))) and recurses once per member, with no depth cap: the skip path does not use zcbor's backup stack, and ZCBOR_MAX_ELEM_COUNT is SIZE_MAX, so nothing bounds how deep the recursion goes. That function is reached on attacker-controlled bytes before any authentication. MCUboot's serial-recovery command parser decodes SMP/CBOR requests with zcbor_map_decode_bulk() (boot/boot_serial/src/zcbor_bulk.c), which skips any map key it does not recognise by calling zcbor_any_skip() on the encoded value; the echo handler in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c calls it directly on the same footing. Both run during image upload, long before the uploaded image's signature is checked. The default receive buffer is MCUBOOT_SERIAL_MAX_RECEIVE_SIZE = 512 bytes and each nesting level costs a single byte to encode (0x81), so roughly 500 levels of nesting fit in one request — comfortably more than a bootloader's stack can absorb, since every frame carries a full zcbor_state_t copy plus locals. The impact is availability only: the bootloader's stack overflows and the device faults or hangs during recovery. There is no controlled out-of-bounds write that escapes the DFU buffer, no disclosure, and no authentication bypass — the recursion grows the stack with the decoder's own internal state. Whether a given board actually exhausts its stack depends on that board's bootloader stack size, which we did not measure; the fix is nevertheless unconditional, because an unauthenticated pre-authentication code path must not have its safety depend on a per-board stack margin. Exposure requires MCUBOOT_SERIAL (serial/SMP recovery), which is not enabled by default, and recovery entry is normally gated on a physical pin (CONFIG_BOOT_SERIAL_ENTRANCE_GPIO / PIN_RESET), with a no-valid-image fallback path. Products that expose serial recovery over an externally reachable transport, or that fall into recovery when no valid image is present, are the ones at risk. The fix is to bound the skip: thread a recursion-depth counter through zcbor_any_skip() (or have zcbor_map_decode_bulk() reject values nested beyond a small constant) and fail once the limit is exceeded — equivalently, take the bounded-skip implementation from upstream zcbor.

t: MCUboot uses assert() as a security guard on the boot/swap/validation path; under NDEBUG (release builds) these checks are compiled out, so an inconsistent/atta
d: Summary MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds. This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites. Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0): boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success). boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend. Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status. Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability). Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure. Reachable-security sites (center the fix here) 1. boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:193 — inconsistent-status assert(0), falls through to complete swap. A2 + !VALIDATE_PRIMARY. [worst] 2. boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:278 — same, swap-offset backend. 3. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:239 — same, swap-scratch backend. 4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL. (Truncated. The full description is in the advisory: https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/security/advisories/GHSA-cr9j-p626-pwcc)

t: Pre-authentication out-of-bounds write in MCUboot encrypted serial recovery image decryption
d: MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer. The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption. A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size. Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144). On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.

t: AutoGPT: Exa Search Monitor triggers skip webhook signature verification and accept forged events
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.11.1 before 0.11.3, anyone with an Exa Search Monitor trigger's URL can start one run of the owner's workflow per request with fake event data, even when a secret is set. The workflow runs with the owner's saved credentials and credits, and nothing is returned to the attacker. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

t: AutoGPT: Cross-origin redirects leak credentials when Location headers contain a backslash
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.1 through 0.10.0, credentials are sent to a third party when a redirect's Location header hides the new host behind a backslash. A signed-in user who connects an MCP server URL, or runs a shared or marketplace workflow with a host-scoped credential, can have that credential delivered to a third party if the host responds with a redirect whose Location the other party influenced. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: AutoGPT: Users can hijack Marketplace listings by adding versions to unowned workflow IDs
d: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.10.0, a user can add a version under another user's workflow ID and take over its Marketplace listing. An attacker with an account and the target's workflow ID can replace the creator's pending Marketplace submission with their own, so that approval installs the attacker's workflow under the creator's listing. Without reviewer involvement, the attacker can also stop the owner from saving new versions and break runs that name no version. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

t: GongShengyue OnlineBooks cross-site request forgery
d: A weakness has been identified in GongShengyue OnlineBooks up to dfc5eacc08d3b0396c266049548618f6fb9587ea. Impacted is an unknown function. This manipulation causes cross-site request forgery. Therefore, version details for affected or updated releases cannot be specified. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
